details:
* Education to pregnant women and families on Meningitis including prevention measures 
* Promoting good nutrition /create awareness on good nutrition for pregnant women 
* Education on good hygiene practice including hand hygiene among pregnant women to prevent meningitis 
* Create awareness among pregnant women on 
  - Information on ANC attendance 
  - Information on the importance of immunization for children 
  - Information/creation of awareness on healthy living
* Sensitize community health workers on meningitis in pregnant women including recognition of the signs and symptoms

* Proper hygiene / handwashing among pregnant women to prevent meningitis 
* Pregnant women to keep away from people who have meningitis.

* Recognition of signs of meningitis in pregnant women such as neck stiffness , neck and /or back pain; and fever
* Urgent referral /transfer to a health facility of pregnant women suspected to have meningitis
* Supportive therapy for pregnant women suspected to have meningitis if urgent transfer is not feasible 
  - Relieve the fever through administration of medication for fever
  - Medication for pain 
  - Encourage fluid intake 
   - Bed rest

Psychosocial  by families and communities support for pregnant women with meningitis and who may develop meningitis complications.

Psychosocial support and counselling for mothers  who  may experience complication s of meningitis including poor foetal outcomes such as loss of the baby (through miscarriage; still births; ); preterm babies; underweight babies

* Create awareness to   families and communities   on meningitis and prevention measures among children under 5 years of age
* Information to the families and communities  on the importance of immunization for children 
* Awareness on good nutrition for children
* Awareness creation to families on hygiene for children
* Provision of IEC materials to communities 
* Community health workers education /sensitization on meningitis and prevention measures

* Vaccination for children under 5 years of age to prevent meningitis 
  - H. influenzae type b vaccine (Hib).
  - Pneumococcal vaccine.  
  - Meningococcal vaccine.  
  - MMR (Measles -mumps -Rubella vaccine);   to prevent viral meningitis                                               
* Proper hygiene / handwashing  for children under 5 years of age to prevent meningitis 
* Keep the children under 5 years of age away from people who have meningitis.

* Recognition of danger signs of meningitis  in infants which include, arching of the back; bulging of fontanelle (the soft spot on the infants head); fever; irritability. 
* Recognition of danger signs of meningitis in children older than 1 year which include, neck stiffness; neck and /or back pain;  fever; seizures
*  Urgent referral /transfer to a health facility of under 5s  suspected to have meningitis
* Supportive therapy for under 5s suspected to have meningitis if   immediate referral  to a health facility is not possible. This includes:. 
  - Give oral fluids
  - Proper feeding for the under 5s with meningitis 
  - Manage fever e.g. through sponging or use of medicines for reducing fever such as paracetamol 
  - Relieve pain through use of medicines for reducing pain (analgesics)  in under 5s with meningitis

* Rehabilitation and follow up of children under 5 years of age with meningitis complications at community level once they are referred down wards from the health facilities     
* Physical therapy to improve motor coordination and mobility
* Occupational therapy to develop everyday skills

* Create awareness to families, communities   and schools on Meningitis and prevention measures among primary school age children 
* Provide information/creation of awareness on healthy living for primary school age children 
* Awareness on good nutrition for primary school age children 
* Provision of IEC materials through schools
* Promote good hygiene practices including hand hygiene  for primary school age children  
* Community health workers education /sensitization on meningitis; recognition of meningitis features  and prevention measures for children

* Proper hygiene / handwashing  
* Keeping away from people who have meningitis
* Vaccination -Meningococcal vaccine.

* Recognition of danger signs of meningitis  in primary school age  children which include, neck stiffness; back pain; fever;  
* Urgent referral of primary school age children suspected to have meningitis
* supportive therapy for school age children suspected to have meningitis if immediate referral to a health facility  is not possible i.e. 
  - Give fluids
  - Proper feeding 
  - Relieve fever through tepid sponging; give antipyretics like paracetamol  
  - Relieve pain through giving analgesics such as paracetamol

* Rehabilitation and follow up of patients at community level once they are referred back from health facilities     
* Physical therapy to improve motor coordination and mobility
* Occupational therapy to develop everyday skills
Psychosocial support and Counselling for the children with meningitis complications and their families

* Create awareness to adolescents and their   families    on meningitis and prevention measures
* Information/creation of awareness on healthy living among the adolescents 
* Awareness on good nutrition for the adolescents 
* Provision of IEC materials 
* Promote good hygiene practices including hand hygiene  for the adolescents

* Practice good hygiene practices including   ‘cough, sneezing etiquette 
* Hand washing with soap and water 
* Limit contact with persons with meningitis

* Recognition of danger signs of meningitis  in adolescents  which include   neck stiffness; neck and/or back pain; fever;
* Urgent referral /transfer to a health facility of adolescents suspected to have meningitis
* Supportive therapy of adolescent suspected to have meningitis if immediate referral is not possible i.e. 
  - Give fluids
  - Proper feeding 
  - Manage fever with antipyretics
Physiotherapy services for adolescents with meningitis complications who may be referred back to communities from health facilities

* Awareness on good nutrition for adults

* Practice good hygiene practices including   ‘cough, sneezing etiquette

* Limit contact with persons with meningitis
